business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation with Fa'amatai customary law and local legislation; company-law statutes follow Commonwealth models)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus) regional free trade agreement, in force for Samoa since 20 December 2020
Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) with Australia
Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) with New Zealand

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2020 (SAM), principally ss. 6 (application), 12-18 (customer due diligence), 21 (beneficial ownership), 35 (PEPs) and 40-48 (record-keeping and reporting); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000 (SAM); Proceeds of Crime Act 2000 (SAM); International Companies Act 1987 (SAM) as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008 and 2011, prescribing registered agent, registered office, register of members and beneficial ownership record-keeping duties; supplementary instruments include the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) AML/CFT compliance directives, the Central Bank of Samoa prudential guidance for payment and remittance service providers, and United Nations Security Council sanctions implementation notices issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (non-public register; beneficial ownership maintained at the licensed registered agent and disclosed to the Registrar of International Companies, the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and law enforcement upon lawful demand; no public search facility)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of each beneficial owner's passport (full color pages)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary public followed by Consular Legalization (Samoa is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (English master version; all-Chinese version permissible as adopted constitutional text with certified English translation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and licensed Samoa registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized execution sheet; no consular legalization required for internal constitutional documents; certified translation mandatory for registry and agent records

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Beneficial Owners for each existing corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or registered agent of the shareholder entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Primary banking institution of the applicant or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized banker's signature; Consular Legalization where the issuing bank or jurisdiction mandates it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / certificate of good conduct for each director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal-records bureau of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the issuing State's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the nearest Samoa diplomatic or consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the licensed Samoa registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Consular Legalization executed in the principal's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under ss. 12-18 of the AML/CFT Act 2020 requires identification and verification of every beneficial owner, director and authorized signatory against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list and Samoa FIU domestic watches/lists. PEPs are screened under FATF Recommendation 12 and require senior management approval, enhanced due diligence and documentary source-of-wealth/source-of-funds evidence. Enhanced Due Diligence applies to this Medium-Risk-Enhanced luxury-resale profile, including provenance documentation for consigned vintage luxury goods and mapping of original transaction flows through target payment rails (Stripe, Escrow-Pay).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - International Company Registry, administered by the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); name clearance applications are lodged exclusively through licensed international company registered agents, with no direct public self-service portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered name must be in English using the Roman (Latin) alphabet. Foreign-script names, including Simplified Chinese, are permissible only as secondary parallel names and must be accompanied by a certified Romanized transliteration for registry records. An all-Chinese Memorandum and Articles of Association may be adopted as the internal constitutional language version, provided a certified English translation is lodged with the registered agent and the Registrar. The name must end with a recognized statutory identifier such as Limited, Ltd, Corporation or an acceptable abbreviation; names suggesting government patronage, unlicensed regulated financial activity, or confusion with an existing registry entry are prohibited.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fund / Mutual Fund / Collective Investment Scheme
Government / Crown / State / Ministry / Authority / National
University / College / Institute / Chamber of Commerce
Samoa International Finance Authority / SIFA or any name implying sponsorship by the Government of Samoa
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or to a protected mark in Samoa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant, acting through its licensed registered agent, must file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, stating the statutory grounds and, where applicable, attaching ministerial consents, disclaimers, corrected transliterations or evidence of distinctiveness from an existing name. The Registrar must determine the appeal within 10 business days. A further administrative appeal lies to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 21 days of the Registrar's decision, and the Minister's determination is final. An amended name application may be refiled without prejudice on the same day, subject to the applicable filing fees under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office without a licensed Samoa registered agent is not permissible; the statutory registered office must be a physical address in Samoa maintained by a licensed agent and used for service of process. Fully remote day-to-day operations are otherwise acceptable for this e-commerce consignment model, with the agent's Apia address serving as the registered office and mail-forwarding base. Payment processors, escrow providers and correspondent banks may nonetheless require enhanced substance evidence, such as executed supply agreements, inventory provenance records and documented operational control from the remote location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a compliant non-resident e-commerce International Company: estimated annual probability below 5% absent an AML/CFT or sanctions risk trigger. Unannounced physical on-site inspections may be conducted by the Registrar or the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit under the AML/CFT Act 2020 where suspicious transactions, sanctions evasion or unauthorized activity are suspected; payment rails (Stripe, Escrow-Pay) typically perform virtual/desk-based merchant reviews rather than physical inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff / prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 4, 5, 9, 10 and 12; Companies Act 2001 (residual general provisions where the International Companies Act is silent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa; administered in coordination with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form 1) under s. 9 of the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; authorized capital may be fixed at USD 1,000,000 with a par value of USD 0.0001 per share. No escrow account or bank deposit requirement applies; capital may be subscribed by a statement of capital filed at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association be and are hereby allotted 1,000 ordinary shares at a par value of USD 0.0001 each, credited as fully paid at incorporation, and that the authorized capital be fixed at USD 1,000,000. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at the office of the Licensed Resident Agent in Apia, Samoa. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the first directors and first secretary be appointed to serve until removed by member resolution, and that the directors be authorized to open bank accounts and activate the Stripe and Escrow-Pay payment rails for the approved luxury consignment e-commerce business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); submitted via the licensed Resident Agent or the SIFA e-Services portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prescribed name reservation application with two proposed company names, together with scanned passport copies and proof of address of each subscriber. Registry will screen the names against the registered names database, protected names, and prohibited words under the International Companies Act 1987. Submission must be made by a SIFA-licensed Resident Agent.
required_dossiers: Utility bill or bank statement evidencing subscriber residential address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for conflict or resemblance, submit an alternative name previously listed in the application, or apply for a fresh reservation with a distinctive suffix such as 'Luxury Resale WS Ltd'.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Samoa, acting together with the licensed Resident Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English using the model forms prescribed under the International Companies Act 1987. The subscribers must execute the Memorandum before a Notary Public, and each proposed director and the secretary must execute consents to act. The documents must include the statement of authorized capital and a registered office address clause.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed and notarized)
Consent to act as director for each appointee
Register of members and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the documents for non-conformity with the prescribed model articles, correct the specified clauses, re-execute the signature pages, and re-submit within the statutory response window of 14 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, the notice of registered office, the Resident Agent's consent, and the statement of authorized capital. No minimum paid-up capital or escrow proof is required; the statement of capital governs initial share allotment.
required_dossiers: Consents of first directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any query letter issued by the Registrar within 14 calendar days, supplying the corrected or supplementary documents; pay the nominal re-assessment fee if the Registry imposes one for excessive requests.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Fees and Stamp Duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL Finance Division and the Treasury of the Government of Samoa, via the SIFA billing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Registry approval, collect the pro-forma invoice for the incorporation fee (USD 200.00) and the first-year annual license fee. Remit the funds by SWIFT bank transfer to the designated government account and upload the payment receipt to the SIFA portal. Stamp duty is waived for International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Remittance advice referencing the Company's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the treasury receipt is not automatically matched, re-attach the SWIFT confirmation to the application reference number and request manual reconciliation through the SIFA help desk within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After fee clearance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, certifies the Memorandum and Articles of Association, and formally files the constitutive documents. The Resident Agent collects the certified originals and issues a digital copy to the shareholders and directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error in the company name or date, file a written rectification request with the Registry and obtain a corrected Certificate; if the Certificate is lost, apply for a duplicate upon affidavit of loss and payment of the replacement fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Resident Agent (SIFA-licensed), in coordination with the Registrar of International Companies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notice of first directors and secretary, open the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges, and registered office), prepare the corporate minute book, and issue share certificates. Obtain a Certificate of Good Standing and ensure the SIFA annual confidentiality filing and annual license fee are settled to maintain the IC's exempt status.
required_dossiers: Notice of First Directors (if not included in Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query is raised on the directors' eligibility or the registered office confirmation, submit corrected declarations within 14 days; late filing penalties are waived if cured within the grace period recognized by the Registrar under the International Companies Act 1987.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the Registrar of International Companies (MCIL) and SIFA supervise the offshore International Company; no industrial licensing board clearance is triggered for the pure e-commerce consignment model operating wholly outside Samoa.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt from local Occupation Permit and Business License — the International Company is authorized under its Certificate of Incorporation to conduct online consignment and secondhand luxury goods retail from outside Samoa; no physical storefront or manufacturing permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Government of Samoa.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category C (low-risk service activity); a full EIA Report is not triggered for digital consignment and resale. Environmental registration is recommended only if the Company later establishes a physical fulfillment warehouse or office within Samoan territory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Nil discharge and emissions liabilities for remote online operations. If a physical facility is opened later, compliance thresholds are: wastewater discharge per the Samoa National Water Quality Standards, VOC and air emission limits per the MNRE interim air quality guidelines, and general waste handling obligations under the Waste Management Act 2010.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety, structural load, or workplace clearance applies to the offshore International Company at the registered office, as the Resident Agent's licensed premises already hold the requisite Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) certification and Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 clearance. Any future on-island display office or warehouse would require an SFESA fire safety certificate and a structural/occupancy approval from PUMA prior to occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa; online taxpayer portal administered by the Ministry for Revenue (formerly Samoa Revenue Authority) at https://www.revenue.gov.ws; all VAGST registrations, filings, and tax returns are processed through the MfR e-services platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) obtains its statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) by filing a 'Company Tax Registration' application with the Ministry for Revenue. Required documents include: (i) Certificate of Incorporation issued under the International Companies Act 1987; (ii) Memorandum and Articles of Association; (iii) registered agent certificate of representation in Samoa (licensed by the Samoa International Finance Authority); (iv) directors and shareholders identification, address, and passport copies; (v) statement of registered office in Samoa. For ICs without public domestic nexus and no income sourced in Samoa, the TIN is issued on a non-resident/tax-exempt designation basis. The Ministry for Revenue issues the TIN electronically within 5-10 business days after submission of a complete application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The International Company is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax under the International Companies Act 1987 and is generally treated as a non-resident company for tax purposes; there is no US-style check-the-box pass-through election. The IC may elect in its constitution to be designated a 'non-resident company' (offshore/exempt) confirming that its commercial activities are conducted exclusively outside Samoa. Hybrid mismatch elections under the Income Tax Act 2019 are unavailable to non-resident exempt companies; a 'resident election' is technically possible only where central management and control are in Samoa, which is generally avoided to preserve tax-exempt status. No entity classification election is required because the IC is taxed at entity level but subject to zero rate of income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (approx. USD 37,000) annual taxable turnover in Samoa. An International Company conducting online resale of vintage luxury goods has VAGST registration obligations only if it makes taxable supplies in Samoa exceeding the WST 100,000 threshold. Supplies by a non-resident IC to customers outside Samoa are outside the scope of VAGST or zero-rated; remote digital/e-commerce services into Samoa are subject to VAGST on the import of services reverse-charge basis where the local recipient is VAT-registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance system or mandatory e-invoicing business-to-government (B2G) API clearance as of 2025. There is no digital stamping requirement for invoices. However, all VAGST-registered persons must file VAGST returns and supporting transactional summaries electronically through the Ministry for Revenue e-services portal. VAGST tax invoices must include prescribed particulars: serial number, date, seller TIN, buyer TIN (where applicable), description, quantity, price, VAGST amount, and the phrase 'Tax Invoice'. The system is audit-based rather than clearance-based; conservation of complete invoice and export records is mandatory to support zero-rating claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating at 0% VAGST applies to: (i) physical export of goods from Samoa where the supplier retains evidence of export within 28 days and title has passed to a non-resident buyer; (ii) supply of a service directly in connection with the export of goods; (iii) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and the benefit of the service occurs wholly outside Samoa; (iv) international transport of goods. For an online reseller of vintage luxury goods, zero rating is available only where physical goods are actually shipped from Samoa to a foreign customer under a valid customs export declaration; consignment or overlapping storage models must be documented with a complete chain of custody.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form Cus-Ex-01) endorsed by Samoa Customs for physical departure of goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing ocean/air export from Samoa to foreign destination
Commercial invoice and purchase/sales documentation evidencing transfer of title and value
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank/escrow settlement statement evidencing foreign currency payment
Packing list and, where applicable, certificate of insurance for the consignment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or unsupported zero-rating claims are treated as tax evasion under the Tax Administration Act 2019 (Samoa). Penalties include: (i) a tax shortfall penalty of 150% of the VAGST avoided; (ii) late payment penalty of 2% per month on the unpaid amount; (iii) statutory interest accruing from the original due date; (iv) retrospective clawback of VAGST for a period of up to 5 years (10 years in cases of fraud or wilful misrepresentation); and (v) criminal sanctions including imprisonment of up to 3 years and fines, with personal liability extending to directors and registered agents who participate in fraudulent exports or sham transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), acting under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1989, the Exchange Control Act 1976, and the Exchange Control Regulations 1980 as the sole administrator of exchange control and monetary oversight in Samoa
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) holds limited but generally workable convertibility for current-account transactions (trade goods, services, interest, dividends, and normal remittances) through licensed commercial banks under delegated CBS authority; capital-account transactions remain subject to prior CBS approval or authorized-dealer consent. An International Company registered under the International Companies Act 1987 is statutorily treated as a non-resident and is expressly exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1976, allowing it to maintain and settle balances in any freely usable currency (USD, EUR, AUD, NZD) without mandatory conversion or CBS capital-account approval. Practical frictions remain: any WST-denominated payment by an IC to a Samoan resident or any Samoan-source settlement routed through a local commercial bank will trigger standard CBS balance-of-payments reporting, threshold-based exchange-control declarations, and enhanced due diligence for luxury goods sellers; profit or capital repatriation to non-resident shareholders, however, faces no legal conversion hurdle because the IC can hold proceeds directly in USD or other foreign currency offshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident exporters, the Exchange Control Regulations require full repatriation of export proceeds within three months of shipment and surrender/ conversion into WST through a licensed commercial bank unless a CBS foreign-currency account permit is obtained. An International Company is exempt from the surrender and repatriation regime by operation of Section 198 of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), so vintage luxury resale receipts collected via offshore payment gateways (Stripe, Escrow Pay) may remain in foreign currency without forced conversion. If, however, the IC chooses to receive WST proceeds from local consignors or settle domestic Samoan expenses in WST, those flows must be cleared through a licensed Samoan bank, which will apply CBS declaration thresholds (above WST 100,000 per transaction or aggregation per month) and suspicious-transaction reporting under the AML/CFT Act 2018.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_notes: Strongest cross-border correspondent network and digital banking platform; accepts International Company accounts with apostilled corporate documents, registered agent certificate, and beneficial-owner KYC; remote opening possible with in-person verification by a director at an ANZ branch in Samoa or via ANZ's Asia-Pacific relationship bank reference.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited (formerly Westpac Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_notes: Maintains the largest local branch network and experienced international corporate onboarding desk; supports USD/WST accounts, SWIFT MT103/MT202, and trade finance (documentary credits) for luxury resale inventories; requires certified board resolution, product authentication policy, and source-of-funds evidence for high-ticket secondhand goods.

Indigenous private bank with growing international corporate focus; viable secondary account for domestic WST settlements consignor payouts; lower correspondent-bank footprint than ANZ/BSP, so USD clearing may involve intermediary charges and longer settlement windows.

State-influenced institution with constrained operational capacity and clarified regulatory oversight; onboards International Companies only with physical presence of directors and substantial local substance evidence; not recommended as primary treasury rail given correspondent and compliance uncertainty.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability. Samoa does not operate a digital EMI licensing regime, and no local fintech can legally provide bank-grade payment/settlement services to an International Company; overseas EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Currenxie) generally decline Samoan ICs due to correspondent-bank risk, FATF-style island-jurisdiction restrictions, and inability to verify the IC's exchange-control exemption in their automated onboarding engines. An offshore EMI can be used only as an ancillary settlement conduit if (a) the IC maintains its primary operational account with a licensed Samoan commercial bank, (b) the EMI is licensed in a reputable jurisdiction (UK FCA, HK MSO, Singapore MAS), and (c) EMI balances are swept daily to the primary bank account; using an unlicensed EMI as principal treasury custodian would breach the AML/CFT Act 2018 reporting-institution mapping and undermine corporate veil protection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is not statutorily mandatory for International Companies, but each licensed bank imposes its own client-onboarding policy: ANZ and BSP allow remote account opening with a hybrid interview (video conference plus notarized/apostilled KYC documents), conditioned on at least one director or the authorized signatory completing an in-person identity verification at a Samoa branch or at a recognized foreign affiliate branch within 90 days; Samoa Commercial Bank requires a physical board-meeting minute and a local registered-agent certificate; National Bank of Samoa requires full physical attendance of all directors and beneficial owners. For a cross-border luxury resale IC with a traditional Chinese family-trust clientele, the lowest-friction route is to appoint a Samoa-registered agent nominee director for local signing while the economic owners execute a properly drafted declaration of trust, and to have one family representative attend a single ANZ/BSP onboarding session in Apia, with documentary notarization thereafter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company with nominee directors, non-resident beneficial owners, and no local office or employees, seeking an operational bank account in a medium-risk AML jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the IC's Memorandum and Articles of Association; certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing from the Samoa Registrar of International Companies; current registered-agent certificate; register of directors and members; signed declaration of trust over nominee shares; passport copies of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) with notarization/apostille; professional source-of-wealth letter (by an accountant/trustee licensed in Samoa or the UBO's home jurisdiction); business plan describing the consignment model, marketplace platforms, and turnover projection; bank and trade references from prior banking relationships; and a completed AML/CFT risk-assessment questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Secondhand luxury goods (ISIC 4791) classified as medium-risk enhanced due diligence: high intrinsic value, portable inventory, potential stolen goods, counterfeit risk, and unidentified drop-shipping counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party authentication certificates (Entrupy, Real Authentication, or certified in-house expert reports) for every luxury item consigned; provable chain-of-custody documentation (consignment agreements, vendor provenance statements, previous sale invoices, lot numbers); insurance coverage certificates for high-value inventory in transit; standardized consignor KYC file (ID, bank account in consignor's name, source-of-goods statement); and a written AML/CFT operational manual covering red flags for luxury resale, including straw-man purchases, rapid buy-sell flip patterns, and payment mirroring anomalies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from family-trust or high-risk-corridor remitters, and outbound funding to marketplace aggregators (Stripe, Escrow Pay) that are not licensed banks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution approving the share-capital subscription and the actual bank wire instruction; SWIFT MT103 records showing remitter name matching the shareholder register; share-allotment certificate and updated share register; CBS inward-investment declaration (Form EBI/FC-FX) filed through the receiving bank; escrow/merchant service agreements with Stripe and Escrow Pay; their regulatory licenses (e.g., FCA/FinCEN/MSB or ASIC-type registrations); monthly escrow settlement reconciliation reports; PCI-DSS and SOC 2 attestations; and a contractual prohibition on cash payments, third-party payouts, or non-identified beneficiary disbursements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity funding must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 (for amounts below USD 10 million) or MT202 for interbank covering, from the shareholder's licensed bank directly to the IC's ANZ/BSP Samoa account or designated foreign-currency account. The remittance must cite CBS balance-of-payments purpose code 1120 (direct investment — equity capital) or 1121 (equity injections) and a plain-text description reading 'Equity subscription — International Company capital — [Company Registration Number]'. The receiving bank will require a CBS Exchange Control declaration (EBI form) where the inward amount exceeds WST 100,000 or where funds originate from a jurisdiction flagged by the Samoa FIU; the bank will also request the share allotment certificate, shareholder register extract, and board resolution within 5 business days of credit. Funds routed through third-party crypto, cash, or non-bank money remitters will be rejected or suspended pending STR filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier and consignor settlements, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 sent from the IC's Samoan or foreign-currency account with purpose code 2110 (trade credit settlement) or 2310 (other goods and services), referencing the commercial invoice and consignment agreement. For large-batch replenishment of authentic vintage inventory (e.g., lots from European auction houses or Japanese luxury dealers), a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by ANZ/BSP under UCP 600 (with advising or confirming bank in the exporter's jurisdiction) ensures title-coupled payment; the required document set is commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill/parcel manifest, independent authentication certificate, insurance certificate, and packing list. E-commerce collections from customers close via Stripe and Escrow Pay settlement rails (card networks, SEPA/ACH, A2A bank debits) and are swept daily to the primary bank account with a 14-day conditional-release window for authentication disputes. Physical inventory movement leverages courier clearing rails (DHL Express, FedEx International Priority, CSV/APAC couriers) with shipment-level value declarations and a customs broker instruction clarifying 'vintage used luxury goods — ISIC 4791' to avoid import misclassification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts with licensed commercial banks (ANZ, BSP) for immediate conversion of USD/EUR/AUD receipts into WST only when domestic settlement is required; International Companies are exempt from mandatory surrender and may keep all FX offshore.

Outright deliverable forwards with maturity not exceeding 12 months for covering current-account payables (consignor settlements in EUR or JPY), obtainable from ANZ/BSP on production of underlying invoices; CBS treats such forwards as legitimate continuous covering and does not require pre-approval for the exempt IC.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible or market-practicable for WST because no recognized offshore deliverable WST market exists; the IC should instead manage exposure by maintaining multi-currency pockets (USD as base, EUR/JPY for purchasing) and matching currency of receivable to currency of payable.

Cross-currency swaps are generally unavailable for International Companies in Samoa; only CBS-licensed banks may execute them, and only for balance-sheet hedging with documented underlying exposure and central-bank approval; speculative swap or option positions are prohibited and would jeopardize the IC's exchange-control exemption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (International Companies Act 2008, s.195) - declaration of registered details, shareholding, and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the annual anniversary of incorporation; market practice requires fee clearance by the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty plus 10% surcharge on unpaid annual fee; prolonged default after written notice permits administrative strike-off; restoration requires court order, arrears, and reinstatement fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee / Continuing Exemption Fee (International Companies Act 2008, s.193)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / Ministry of Finance, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the incorporation anniversary each year; 30-day grace period before penalty accrual
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% penalty if unpaid 30 days after due date; continued non-payment triggers administrative strike-off and suspension of tax-exempt status until reinstated

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Attestation (UBO register confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (regulated by Samoa International Finance Authority) and Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneous with Annual Return; Register of Members and UBO Register must be updated within 30 days of any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or incomplete UBO attestation attracts monetary penalties and possible director disqualification; defective registers invalidate the Annual Return

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certificate of Good Standing (optional; commercially required for Stripe, Escrow-Pay, and banking due-diligence revalidation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued on demand, typically within 2-5 business days after annual fee clearance; request annually for processor/bank reviews
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not a statutory filing; non-issuance indicates unpaid Government Fee and imminent administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit-exempt for a standard non-licensed International Company. Mandatory independent audit applies only if the IC (i) holds a financial services licence (banking, insurance, or trust business), (ii) is listed or makes a public offering, or (iii) shareholders by special resolution or the constitution require an audit. A vintage luxury resale e-commerce IC not licensed in Samoa remains statutorily audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No public filing of financial statements required for exempt ICs. Where accounts are prepared (e.g., for lender or payment-processor underwriting), statements must follow IFRS or other recognized accounting standards as resolved by the board and be retained at the registered office in Samoa.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent maintains the Beneficial Ownership Register and annually attests its accuracy within the Annual Return. Any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and mirrored in the UBO Register before the annual confirmation; the agent must be notified of a transfer within 30 days. Samoa imposes no public UBO filing, but the attested register must be made available to the Registrar and Samoan authorities upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) with full transfer history
Register of Charges (if any security interests are granted)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,000 per annum (licensed registered agent service, inclusive of registered office, annual return preparation, and UBO register maintenance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 - statutorily exempt; voluntary certified audit for payment-processor underwriting USD 1,500 - 3,500; compilation-only financial statements USD 800 - 1,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (resident corporate income tax on Samoan-source income); a non-resident International Company is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax and bears an effective rate of 0% on its foreign-source vintage luxury resale profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The International Company enjoys a statutory 100% income tax exemption under Section 187 of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended in 2018), read together with Section 5(1)(c) of the Income Tax Act 2015 (foreign-source income exclusion). A formal tax exemption certificate is issued by the Registrar of International Companies at incorporation. No Samoan corporate income tax, capital gains tax, dividend withholding tax, or estate duty applies to an IC that does not carry on business in Samoa and does not derive Samoan-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (IC Return Form G-100) together with the Annual Government Fee Schedule, administered under the International Companies Act 1987 (amended 2018) and the Companies Act 2006. Filing is made through the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Companies Registry E-Registry portal, or by the licensed Samoa-registered agent on behalf of the IC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return must be filed within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation stated on the Certificate of Incorporation. The Annual Government Fee is payable on or before the same filing anniversary; failure to pay the fee within 6 months triggers automatic strike-off procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company as it appears on the Certificate of Incorporation, including any name suffix indicating limited liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered English or romanized Chinese name; do not use a name that implies a Samoan domestic trading company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique International Company registration number issued by the MCIL Companies Registry at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Copy the number from the Certificate of Incorporation; used for all subsequent fee, tax, and banking references.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of issuance of the certificate; fixes the annual filing anniversary cycle.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC that has changed its registered agent must still file by the original anniversary date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, license number, and address of the Samoa-licensed registered agent mandated under Section 118 of the International Companies Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent is the IC's statutory address for all official notifications and must be a person licensed by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the registered office in Samoa, which must be located at the registered agent's licensed premises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A post office box alone is insufficient; the address must permit service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description or ISIC/NAICS classification of the IC's main commercial purpose as stated in its charter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For this vehicle, enter 'Online consignment and secondhand luxury goods retail' (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 459510). Avoid any wording indicating domestic Samoan retail activity, which would violate the IC's non-resident trading restriction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether any income is derived from sources within Samoa during the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC must answer 'No' and confirm it has not carried on business in Samoa. All consignment, marketplace, and payment-rail revenues are to be characterized as foreign-source for Samoan tax purposes. This declaration governs eligibility for the tax exemption certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, nationalities, and residential addresses of directors (minimum one natural person) and any corporate secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors may be used, but beneficial ownership must be disclosed to the registered agent and entered in the confidential Beneficial Ownership Register maintained under the 2018 amendments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory levy calculated from the IC's authorized share capital, payable concurrently with the Annual Return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee brackets range approximately from WST 800 to WST 4,000 equivalent; payment is made by bank draft or electronic transfer through the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate signed by a director or the registered agent attesting to the accuracy of the return and continued compliance with the International Companies Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Falsification of this declaration is a perjury offense under Section 228 of the Act; a director resident outside Samoa may execute the form by digital signature transmitted to the agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file within the statutory period incurs a late filing penalty of WST 500 per month or part thereof, capped in the Registrar's discretion. Non-payment of the Annual Government Fee for more than six months exposes the IC to strike-off from the International Companies register under Section 130, with a reinstatement fee of WST 1,000 plus arrears. Officers who knowingly sign a false return are liable to fines of up to WST 100,000 and two years' imprisonment under Section 228, and the tax exemption certificate may be revoked retroactively.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Samoa's domestic dividend withholding tax rate is 15% for non-resident shareholders, but it applies only to dividends sourced in Samoa. A non-resident International Company distributing profits accumulated from foreign-source e-commerce turnover is outside the Samoan dividend withholding net; the effective rate is 0%. Under the Samoa-New Zealand Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the residual Samoan rate is 15% (5% where the recipient is a company holding 10% or more of the voting power); the Samoa-Australia DTA allows 15% (5% for a company owning at least 10% of the voting power). These treaty rates are irrelevant to a tax-exempt IC making a pure non-Samoan distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's Ministry of Revenue (Inland Revenue Division) administers the limited DTA network (currently Australia and New Zealand). To invoke treaty relief, the payor's registered agent must (i) submit a DTA application form not less than 30 days before the distribution date; (ii) obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Ministry of Revenue certifying the IC's exempt non-resident status, which will generally be issued only when the IC has no Samoan-source income; (iii) obtain the beneficial owner's TRC from the Australian or New Zealand competent authority; (iv) provide a statement that the IC is not a conduit arrangement and that the shareholder is the beneficial owner; and (v) retain all TRCs, certificates of exemption, and board minutes on file for six years. The tax exemption certificate of the IC is not a substitute for a TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Samoan withholding tax is 15% on royalties and 15% on interest paid by a Samoan resident to a non-resident. For a tax-exempt International Company, payments of brand license royalties, platform certification fees, or interest on shareholder loans funded from foreign-source receivables are not subject to Samoan deduction withholding because the IC is non-resident for tax purposes and the payment has no Samoan-source character. Under the Samoa-New Zealand DTA, interest is capped at 10% and royalties at 10%; under the Samoa-Australia DTA, interest is capped at 10% and royalties at 10%. Where the luxury resale vehicle holds a trademark or software license from an associated Hong Kong or EU company, the payment should be structured and documented as an arm's length cost of sales in the IC's contemporaneous transfer pricing file.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 2,000,000 (approximately USD 760,000) of aggregate related-party transactions in a tax year triggers the obligation to prepare and retain a Local File under Samoa's Income Tax (Transfer Pricing) Rules; a Master File is required where the consolidated global group turnover of the IC and its associates exceeds WST 50,000,000, or where the group satisfies the OECD materiality threshold for the Master File. A non-resident International Company that does not carry on business in Samoa and derives no Samoan-source income is generally outside the domestic documentation obligation, but the parent group must nevertheless maintain a full transfer pricing file at its foreign headquarters, anchored by a resale-price or transactional-net-margin analysis supporting the IC's commission on the online luxury resale transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicability of Economic Substance Regulations (ESR): Samoa enacted the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2021, operative from 1 July 2021, in alignment with the OECD Forum on Harmful Tax Practices and EU listing standards. An International Company carrying on a relevant activity, expressly including distribution and service, intellectual property holding, and pure equity holding, must demonstrate economic presence in Samoa. The doctrine requires: (i) board or senior management meetings held in Samoa; (ii) the engagement of an appropriately qualified Samoan resident officer or manager; (iii) a physical registered office staffed to perform core income-generating activities (CIGA); and (iv) adequacy of Samoan expenditure proportionate to the IC's income. For the vintage luxury resale vehicle, the CIGA are inventory sourcing, consignment listing, payment processing, and logistics orchestration through foreign online marketplaces; the IC must be able to prove that any claimed exemption does not rest solely on the Samoan tax status, and must keep board minutes, substance declarations, and outsourced service agreements at the registered office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking the entire commercial operating profit of the online secondhand luxury resale business into a tax-exempt Samoa International Company while the true management, sellers, inventory, and decision makers remain in a high-tax home territory, without a bona fide agency arrangement with the foreign marketplace operator and without transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015, deliberate evasion attracts a shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax avoided plus late payment interest at 6.3% per annum; the International Companies Act Section 204 imposes fines of up to WST 100,000 on officers for filing false returns; the Ministry of Revenue may revoke the tax exemption certificate retrospectively and the entire exempt period may be re-assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under the common-law sham doctrine; directors and the beneficial owner are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, any penalties, and the IC's debts if the entity is insolvent. Directors may be made subject to departure prohibition orders, travel bans, and asset freezing orders under the Tax Administration Act, and on criminal conviction face imprisonment of up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-filing of the economic substance declaration under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2021; absence of board minutes; no Samoa-resident officer; no locally performed management functions; reliance exclusively on the registered agent's mailbox and the statutory tax exemption; or the use of a single agent for a fleet of similar e-commerce ICs without differentiated substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of WST 10,000 per relevant activity per fiscal year, a daily default penalty of WST 500 for continued non-compliance, and a mandatory strike-off order from the Companies Registry. The Registrar may also exchange information automatically with the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction under Samoa's participation in the OECD Global Forum and the Pacific Islands Tax Administration exchange network.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Court may enter a personal contribution order against the directors and registered agent for the company's unpaid penalties where the IC has been dissolved; individual directors may be disqualified from acting as corporate officers in Samoa for up to five years, and licensed agents may be debarred, which in practice freezes the IC's bank accounts and Stripe/Escrow payouts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the luxury resale and consignment business without customer due diligence on third-party consignors, such that Escrow-Pay and Stripe rails commingle proceeds of dozens of unrelated sellers through an omnibus account; accepting transfers from unvetted money-service businesses; failing to file suspicious transaction reports with the Financial Intelligence Unit; or receiving proceeds from the sale of stolen high-value vintage goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AML/CTF Act 2007 (as amended 2017) imposes civil penalties of up to WST 2,000,000 on the entity and its principals for institutional non-compliance; the Proceeds of Crime Act 2016 authorizes forfeiture and confiscation of the entire luxury goods inventory if the assets derive from predicate offences; the Financial Intelligence Unit may restrict the IC's bank accounts and report the entity to international financial intelligence networks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and accountable persons face criminal fines and imprisonment of up to 14 years for money laundering, structuring, or false AML/CTF declarations; travel bans, passport seizure, asset freezing, and the blocking of all payment rails follow as statutory incident relief; the personal assets of controllers may be confiscated under the proceeds-of-crime framework.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying the associated Hong Kong or EU marketplace operator a below-arm's-length commission or receiving inventory through a related-party luxury-certification intermediary at inflated prices, enabling the tax-exempt Samoa IC to capture artificial margins; absence of contemporaneous CUP or resale price evidence in the side ledger; or issuing retroactive intercompany invoices during a tax dispute.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Income Tax (Transfer Pricing) Rules and Section 67 of the Income Tax Act 2015 authorize the Commissioner to adjust the consideration to arm's length, impose a 40% uplift penalty on the adjusted amount, and levy gross-rated failure penalties of WST 50,000 for non-production of documentation, plus late payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the adjustment creates a tax debt that the IC cannot pay, the Commissioner may pursue directors under the voidable-arrangement provisions; personal liability attaches for the adjusted tax; directors face departure bans from Samoa until the debt is settled, and enforcement may be directed against the IC's bank accounts and the Escrow balances held for the associated buyers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Registry False Return / Fraud and Beneficial Ownership Non-Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Stating 'no business activity' on the Annual Return while actively operating the e-commerce site; failing to record the natural-person beneficial owner of the IC in the Confidential Beneficial Ownership Register introduced by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018; or providing false particulars of incorporation continuation to the MCIL E-Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 228 of the International Companies Act 1987 imposes a fine of up to WST 50,000 and two years' imprisonment on officers for knowing false statements; the Registrar may strike-off the company and report the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit; the IC's bank and escrow accounts may be frozen pending correction of the beneficial ownership record.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal conviction, automatic disqualification from managing any Samoan company for five years, and joint and several liability with the company for all outstanding fees, penalties, and tax liabilities; the disqualification order extends to the director's capacity as trustee of any associated family trust holding the IC shares.
